## Simultaneous Global Shock

Major global bond markets are experiencing simultaneous shocks as interest rates surge across the United States, Japan, and the United Kingdom following Korea's announcement of its largest-ever fiscal expansion package. The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield jumped 0.05 percentage points to 4.80%, reaching its highest level in one year and eight months since January of last year. This bond market turbulence stems from a combination of factors including escalating U.S.-Iran military tensions in the Middle East and fiscal pressures facing European Union nations. Oil prices are surging alongside the heightened geopolitical risks, creating a perfect storm for global financial markets and raising concerns that South Korea's government bond yields may remain elevated for an extended period.

## August Inflation Acceleration

South Korea's consumer price inflation rate rebounded to 3.1% in August, marking a return to the 3% level after just two months, up from 2.8% in July. This acceleration is primarily driven by a base effect from last year's SK Telecom mobile phone rate reductions, which saw telecommunications costs spike 26.7% year-over-year. Core inflation, which excludes volatile items, climbed to 3.4%, the highest reading in three years and three months. Service prices rose 3.7% and industrial products increased 3.7%, indicating broad-based price pressures across the economy. The Bank of Korea has indicated that September consumer prices will likely maintain this upward trajectory centered on core items, reinforcing concerns about persistent inflation despite the government's expansionary fiscal stance.

## Interest Rate Pressures Globally

The Bank of Korea itself raised its benchmark rate to 3% through consecutive hikes in July and August, with the central bank now signaling that momentum will continue given inflation concerns. Meanwhile, New Zealand's central bank independently raised its official cash rate by 0.25 percentage points from 2.5% to 2.75%, demonstrating that rate-hiking central banks worldwide are coordinating efforts to combat inflation. The CME FedWatch tool shows that markets now price in a 68% probability of a U.S. Federal Reserve rate increase in September, up sharply from expectations just days earlier. This represents a dramatic shift in market sentiment away from rate cuts, putting significant pressure on equity markets globally and creating headwinds for growth-sensitive stocks.

## Stock Market Turbulence

The KOSPI plummeted 3.99% as foreign investors fled Asian markets amid escalating U.S. Treasury yield concerns and rising oil prices. The index fell sharply to the 6,500 level, with major semiconductor names taking particular losses as semiconductor bellwether SK Hynix declined 4.73%. The KOSDAQ also struggled, falling 2.1% to close at 803.98, reflecting selling pressure across growth-oriented technology stocks. Meanwhile, the Korean won weakened slightly by 1.7 won to settle at 1,368.7 per U.S. dollar. Market volatility has intensified significantly as investors grapple with the dual headwinds of rising interest rates and geopolitical risks. The combination of higher bond yields and Middle East tensions is creating a risk-off environment that has been particularly punishing for equity markets.

## Fiscal Expansion Amid Economic Headwinds

Despite the government's mega fiscal package announcement, policymakers face mounting pressure to control inflation without triggering a credit event. Government officials argue that the debt-to-GDP ratio is projected to reach 49% by the end of the current administration, improving by 10 percentage points from initial expectations, thereby demonstrating improved fiscal health. However, critics point out that expanding fiscal stimulus during inflationary periods risks further overheating the economy and complicating monetary policy normalization. The government is preparing additional price stabilization measures ahead of the Chuseok holiday period to demonstrate commitment to price control.

## Housing Market Adjustments

The government reversed its plan to reduce the comprehensive property tax basic deduction for non-resident single-property owners, maintaining the current 1.2 billion won threshold. However, experts note this provides only temporary relief without addressing fundamental supply issues in the rental market. Seoul monthly rent listings have declined 12.8% and jeonse listings down 11.9% over the past year, reflecting severe market stress. Samsung Electronics has begun offering unprecedented 1.5% interest rate housing loans up to 500 million won for unmarried employees starting September, potentially stimulating demand in the semiconductor belt areas around Dongtan. This low-cost financing, exempt from debt-service-ratio regulations, is already generating significant inquiries among real estate brokers.

## Agricultural Budget Surge

The Ministry of Agriculture is deploying surging rural special tax revenues to eliminate approximately 3.1 trillion won in accumulated public fund management debts while consolidating three agricultural funds into one. Next year's agricultural and rural financing will increase 25.7%, marking the largest year-over-year increase on record. Rural special tax collections have surged 180% over the past year, providing the financial resources for this unprecedented budgetary expansion in the agricultural sector. This consolidation represents a major restructuring of rural development infrastructure.

## Global Trade and AI Competition

The United States is intensifying pressure on G20 nations to eliminate AI regulations and conform to America-centered AI ecosystem standards. Simultaneously, the U.S. is pursuing aggressive tariff policies while seeking allied cooperation on China containment. AI token prices have plummeted to historic lows, with OpenAI and Anthropic implementing discounts up to 45% for enterprise customers in response to aggressive Chinese competition. The LLM token expenditure index fell to 0.97 dollars per million tokens, representing a 50% decline from its May peak of 2.05 dollars. While lower prices reduce adoption barriers, experts warn this pricing war threatens the financial sustainability of AI companies long-term.

## Investment Implications

For investors, the current environment presents significant crosscurrents requiring careful navigation. Bond yields rising to multi-month highs make fixed-income investments more attractive, yet equity volatility remains elevated amid persistent inflation concerns and geopolitical risks. Growth stocks, particularly in technology and semiconductors, face continued pressure as interest rate expectations shift higher. Domestic consumption may face headwinds from elevated inflation and potential rate maintenance at elevated levels. The housing market presents mixed signals, with certain regional markets benefiting from corporate housing programs while overall market stress remains pronounced. International investors should monitor the Middle East situation closely, as further escalation could trigger additional commodity and bond market shocks, while Korean exporters face headwinds from both strong dollar dynamics and weakening global demand.
headline: Global Bond Tantrum Hits Markets as Korea Unveils Mega Fiscal Expansion
